farm_description: potatoes in thika leaves are turning brown

diagnosis.summary: Your potato plants in Thika are suffering from browning leaves, which threatens the harvest.
likely_causes: Late blight, a serious disease that spreads rapidly during wet weather.
Early blight, which causes dark brown spots on older leaves first.
Lack of enough water or soil nutrients to support healthy leaf growth.
diagnosis.recommended_approach: Immediately remove and destroy affected leaves to stop the spread. Space your plants well and apply low-cost copper-based fungicides or wood ash to protect the remaining crop.

this_week_actions: Cut off all brown or spotted potato leaves and bury them deep in the ground far from your field.
Dust the remaining healthy potato leaves with dry wood ash early in the morning while there is still dew.
Clear all weeds around the potato plants to improve airflow and keep the leaves dry.
Spray the remaining crop with a copper-based fungicide if the weather remains wet and rainy.
materials_needed: Dry wood ash collected from your kitchen fireplace.
Clean pruning shears or a sharp knife disinfected with rubbing alcohol.
Copper-based fungicide purchased from your local agrovet shop.
warning_signs: The plant stems turn black and mushy within a few days.
Entire potato plants wilt and collapse despite soil being moist.
action_plan.expected_outcome: The spread of brown spots will stop, and your plants will show healthy green leaf growth within two weeks.
